name: Hardening, recovery, migrations and scalability
scope: Implement crash recovery/reconciliation for state/receipt/baseline/event operations.
Implement migration framework for persisted schemas.
Benchmark and optimize dependency graph/diff/materialization on synthetic large projects.
Evaluate optional watch mode only after explicit-command semantics are stable.
out_of_scope: LLM semantic reviewer embedded into engine core.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Crash-injection tests do not leave contradictory state/receipt/baseline/event combinations.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Post-axis dev15 corrections strengthen corrupt-journal preflight and preserve recovery evidence after rollback failure.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Concurrent writers are serialized or rejected clearly; readers do not observe partially committed state.
acceptance_criteria.notes: P7 hardening scope verified; global release consolidation remains P8.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Migration fixtures preserve or explicitly transform receipts/baselines/history with version checks.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Post-axis dev15 migration validates released evidence and registry/event provenance before marking current layout.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Recovery can diagnose and reconcile interrupted operations with an auditable event.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Hardening audit logs are strict verification evidence; corrupt history blocks verification.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Declared synthetic scale benchmark meets the recorded performance budget or phase remains partial.
acceptance_criteria.notes: P7-A5 is deliberately partial under answered Q7.3; environment-normalized budget becomes blocking before P8 acceptance.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Hardening changes do not alter user-visible semantics from accepted earlier phases without corresponding contract/migration updates.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Post-axis dev15 package audit, wheel/source parity and manifest-only portable-copy regression confirm no unintended user-visible semantic regression; DAX18 remains separately partial by design.

pre_execution_questions.question: Какую concurrency model фиксируем для первого hardened release?
pre_execution_questions.why_it_matters: Runtime state is file-based; uncontrolled multi-writer access risks corruption.
pre_execution_questions.recommended_default: Single writer per documentation root via lock; concurrent read-only commands allowed when safe.
pre_execution_questions.answer: Single writer per documentation root via lock; concurrent read-only commands allowed when safe.
pre_execution_questions.decision: Adopt this implementation default for v0.1 unless implementation evidence exposes a contradiction.
pre_execution_questions.acceptance_impact: Must be resolved before phase acceptance.

pre_execution_questions.question: Когда обязательна migration, а когда допустим reset runtime state?
pre_execution_questions.why_it_matters: Baselines/receipts may be valuable audit evidence and should not disappear silently.
pre_execution_questions.recommended_default: Canonical/document data never reset. Persisted dependency state formats require migrations once released; reset allowed only for explicitly disposable caches, not receipts/history/baselines.
pre_execution_questions.answer: Canonical/document data never reset. Persisted dependency state formats require migrations once released; reset allowed only for explicitly disposable caches, not receipts/history/baselines.
pre_execution_questions.decision: Adopt this implementation default for v0.1 unless implementation evidence exposes a contradiction.
pre_execution_questions.acceptance_impact: Must be resolved before phase acceptance.

pre_execution_questions.question: Какой synthetic scale и performance budget принять?
pre_execution_questions.recommended_default: Start benchmark fixture at 10k resources / 50k dependency edges; establish measured baseline in P8, then record an environment-normalized budget before acceptance.
pre_execution_questions.answer: Start benchmark fixture at 10k resources / 50k dependency edges; establish measured baseline in P8, then record an environment-normalized budget before acceptance.
pre_execution_questions.decision: Adopt this implementation default for v0.1 unless implementation evidence exposes a contradiction.
pre_execution_questions.acceptance_impact: Non-blocking until benchmark baseline is measured; becomes blocking before P8 acceptance.

pre_execution_questions.question: Нужен ли watch mode вообще в v0.x?
pre_execution_questions.why_it_matters: It adds background behavior that is less transparent for AI and CI.
pre_execution_questions.recommended_default: Keep optional and out of acceptance unless explicit-command workflow proves insufficient.
pre_execution_questions.answer: Keep optional and out of acceptance unless explicit-command workflow proves insufficient.
pre_execution_questions.decision: Adopt this implementation default for v0.1 unless implementation evidence exposes a contradiction.
pre_execution_questions.acceptance_impact: Does not block P8 unless user promotes watch mode into scope.

emergent_questions.question: Should recognized P6 runtime evidence require a separate manual migration before every P7 mutation?
emergent_questions.why_it_matters: Blocking all accepted P6 workflows on a manual step would change behavior unnecessarily when the migration is byte-preserving and deterministic.
emergent_questions.recommended_default: No. Keep explicit `migrate`, but allow recognized P6 layout to migrate automatically inside the same exclusive transaction before a normal mutation.
emergent_questions.answer: No. Keep explicit `migrate`, but allow recognized P6 layout to migrate automatically inside the same exclusive transaction before a normal mutation.
emergent_questions.decision: Recognized legacy P6 layout auto-migrates transactionally; unknown/future versions still fail and are never reset.

emergent_questions.question: Where should the per-documentation-root lock live if read-only commands must not mutate the project?
emergent_questions.why_it_matters: A project-local lock file would violate the accepted read-only file-tree guarantee merely by observing the project.
emergent_questions.recommended_default: Use an OS-temporary lock path keyed by the resolved documentation root.
emergent_questions.answer: Use an OS-temporary lock path keyed by the resolved documentation root.
emergent_questions.decision: P7 uses an external OS lock; project-owned transaction/recovery evidence is created only by mutations.
emergent_questions.acceptance_impact: DAX15/DAX12 compatibility with P6 read-only contract.

emergent_questions.question: What should automatic recovery do if a transaction target changed outside the interrupted transaction after the crash?
emergent_questions.why_it_matters: Blind rollback could destroy a legitimate post-crash edit, while silently accepting the edit could leave a partially committed transaction.
emergent_questions.recommended_default: Refuse automatic overwrite. Allow explicit `recover --force` to choose pre-crash rollback, and audit the forced conflict paths.
emergent_questions.answer: Refuse automatic overwrite. Allow explicit `recover --force` to choose pre-crash rollback, and audit the forced conflict paths.
emergent_questions.decision: Default recovery preserves unknown bytes and remains pending; `--force` is an explicit destructive operator decision recorded in recovery history.

emergent_questions.question: How can a transaction preserve read-your-writes while still recovering from a process crash?
emergent_questions.why_it_matters: Pure staging would require every store read to virtualize staged files; immediate writes without journaling would expose unrecoverable partial state after a crash.
emergent_questions.recommended_default: Use an exclusive lock plus durable pre-images/planned hashes before each immediate atomic file write. Readers cannot enter during the writer; recovery rolls back open journals.
emergent_questions.answer: Use an exclusive lock plus durable pre-images/planned hashes before each immediate atomic file write. Readers cannot enter during the writer; recovery rolls back open journals.
emergent_questions.decision: P7 uses write-ahead pre-images with immediate atomic writes under the exclusive lock; journal commit defines command durability.

emergent_questions.question: Should a P6 runtime containing only materialization provenance be treated as empty when no dependency receipts/state exist?
emergent_questions.why_it_matters: Materialization provenance is released persisted evidence and must be included in migration detection/preservation.
emergent_questions.recommended_default: No. `materialization_state.json` alone makes the unmarked runtime a legacy P6 layout that requires the registered migration.
emergent_questions.answer: No. `materialization_state.json` alone makes the unmarked runtime a legacy P6 layout that requires the registered migration.
emergent_questions.decision: Migration detection includes materialization state and the migration preservation digest covers it.

emergent_questions.question: Does a leftover journal with durable `phase=committed` represent a recovery blocker?
emergent_questions.why_it_matters: The commit marker defines durability; treating cleanup-only residue as partial state would incorrectly block safe readers.
emergent_questions.recommended_default: No. Committed residue is a non-blocking cleanup warning; readers may proceed and `recover`/the next writer removes it.
emergent_questions.answer: No. Committed residue is a non-blocking cleanup warning; readers may proceed and `recover`/the next writer removes it.
emergent_questions.decision: Read guard blocks only uncommitted journals; verify reports `transaction_cleanup_required` warning for committed residue.

emergent_questions.question: How strict must the runtime-layout marker parser be relative to its JSON Schema?
emergent_questions.why_it_matters: A weak parser could silently accept corrupted migration provenance and recreate the schema/runtime mismatch class found in earlier phases.
emergent_questions.recommended_default: Enforce schema-critical keys/types/provenance/digests/timestamps and reject unknown keys/future versions.
emergent_questions.answer: Enforce schema-critical keys/types/provenance/digests/timestamps and reject unknown keys/future versions.
emergent_questions.decision: Runtime layout loading now validates the same audit-critical constraints as the schema before treating the layout as current.

emergent_questions.question: How can P7 complete when P7-A5 says the phase remains partial without a performance budget, Q7.3 defers that budget to P8, P8 says it starts only after P7 acceptance, and the phase schema has no partial status?
emergent_questions.why_it_matters: Without an explicit handoff rule the phase graph deadlocks or silently loses the DAX18 release obligation.
emergent_questions.recommended_default: Accept the completed P7 hardening scope with DAX18 explicitly partial, carry DAX18 as a blocking P8 release-gate axis, and require an environment-normalized budget plus passing benchmark before P8 acceptance.
emergent_questions.answer: Accept P7 hardening with DAX18 explicitly partial and promote DAX18 into P8 as a blocking release-gate item.
emergent_questions.decision: P7 may be phase-accepted with P7-A5/DAX18 partial because Q7.3 intentionally defers the threshold. P8 acceptance axes now include DAX18 and P8-A8 requires a recorded normalized budget and passing benchmark before final release acceptance.
emergent_questions.acceptance_impact: Resolves the P7→P8 process deadlock without pretending DAX18 passed. P8 cannot be accepted until DAX18 is closed.

emergent_questions.question: May recovery execute a transaction journal that is syntactically/schema-valid but semantically inconsistent with its directory, pre-images, or current filesystem state?
emergent_questions.why_it_matters: Recovery instructions are destructive authority. A semantically impossible journal must not be allowed to select files for deletion/restoration merely because its JSON shape validates.
emergent_questions.recommended_default: No. Recovery must fail closed: validate transaction-directory identity, journal invariants, pre-image existence/hash relationships and current/planned hashes before the first rollback mutation. Preserve corrupt evidence for diagnosis.
emergent_questions.answer: No. Corrupt or semantically impossible journals are never executable recovery instructions.
emergent_questions.decision: Recovery fully validates the journal and all operations before changing files; transaction-id/path mismatches, impossible existed/backup/hash relationships and rogue transaction entries remain `recovery_required` without mutation.
emergent_questions.acceptance_impact: Resolved post-acceptance DAX14/DAX15 destructive-recovery defect; no user decision required.

emergent_questions.question: Can a runtime-layout marker self-assert migration provenance, or must migrated_from/migration_id correspond to the registered migration and validated released evidence?
emergent_questions.why_it_matters: A self-asserted marker could make corrupt or unknown legacy evidence appear migrated/current and bypass DAX16 compatibility guarantees.
emergent_questions.recommended_default: Migration provenance is registry-bound. A migrated marker is valid only when its from/to/id tuple matches a registered migration and released evidence passes the migration validator; unknown provenance is invalid.
emergent_questions.answer: Migration provenance is registry-bound, not self-authenticating.
emergent_questions.decision: Runtime-layout loading validates migrated provenance against `MIGRATIONS.json`/runtime registry; migration refuses symlinked or structurally/integrity-corrupt released evidence and never writes a current marker on failure.

emergent_questions.question: Are P7 migration/recovery audit logs themselves verification evidence, or may corrupt logs be ignored once the runtime files look usable?
emergent_questions.why_it_matters: P7 promises auditable recovery/migration. Ignoring corrupt audit logs would make that history unverifiable and allow `verify` to report a clean runtime with damaged provenance.
emergent_questions.recommended_default: Treat hardening audit logs as verification evidence. Malformed/schema-invalid records are blocking verification findings; verify must still return a complete report rather than crash.
emergent_questions.answer: Hardening audit logs are verification evidence and corruption is blocking.
emergent_questions.decision: `verify` validates migration/recovery JSONL records and reports corruption through the complete-report envelope; corrupt dependency receipts similarly remain report findings rather than exit-5 internal errors.
emergent_questions.acceptance_impact: Resolved DAX14 diagnostics/auditability and P6 complete-report regression.

implementation_log.entry: Implemented external shared-reader/exclusive-writer lock keyed by documentation root; lock files live outside the project tree.
Implemented write-ahead rollback transactions with durable pre-images/planned hashes for dependency and materialization writes.
Implemented crash recovery with auditable recovery events, default conflict refusal and explicit `recover --force`.
Implemented runtime-layout migration registry, P6 byte-preserving migration, explicit `migrate`, and transactional auto-migration of recognized legacy layout before mutation.
Added 10k-target/50k-edge scalability baseline plus 10k structured diffs and 10k deterministic Markdown renders.
Kept filesystem watch/daemon mode out of P7 acceptance per Q7.4; explicit CLI remains canonical.
acceptance correction: first P7 mutation initializes runtime-layout provenance in the same transaction so a fresh runtime does not become false legacy on the next command.
axis correction: materialization-only P6 runtime is detected as legacy evidence and migrated/preserved, not treated as empty.
axis correction: committed-but-not-cleaned transaction journals are safe cleanup warnings rather than recovery blockers.
axis correction: runtime layout parser enforces schema-critical migration provenance instead of checking version alone.
acceptance correction: resolved P7/P8 performance-gate deadlock by carrying partial DAX18 explicitly into P8 and making normalized-budget benchmark closure mandatory before P8 acceptance.
post-axis correction: recovery now strictly validates transaction journals/roots and preflights all operations before target mutation; semantically impossible journals cannot delete existing files.
post-axis correction: failed synchronous rollback preserves journal/pre-images instead of deleting the only recovery evidence.
post-axis correction: migration rejects symlinked/corrupt released evidence and cross-validates current migration provenance against registry and audit history.
post-axis correction: verify includes strict hardening recovery/migration audit history and contains corrupt receipt evidence inside verification findings instead of exit-5 internal failure.
post-axis correction: active P7 runtime/materialization documentation and self-audit are synchronized with the accepted hardening boundary.
post-axis correction: recovery validates complete journal semantics before any mutation; corrupt/rogue/id-mismatched journals fail closed and are preserved for diagnosis.
post-axis correction: external deletion after crash is treated as an unknown post-crash change and requires explicit audited `recover --force`.
post-axis correction: runtime-layout schema/runtime/registry provenance agree; migration rejects symlinked or integrity-corrupt released evidence.
post-axis correction: verify contains corrupt receipt/hardening audit-log failures inside the complete verification report instead of internal-error or silent omission.
post-axis handoff correction: active P7 docs/source README/CLI fallback are synchronized to P7 and self-audit guards against regression.

findings: Recovery and migration produce auditable events; unresolved crash journals are diagnosable via verify/recover.
Committed cleanup-only journals are non-blocking warnings; forced conflict rollback is explicit and auditable.
Post-axis dev15: recovery/migration audit histories are strictly parsed, failed rollback preserves evidence, and corrupt receipts remain inside complete verification reports.
Post-axis: corrupt journals/audit logs/receipts now fail closed and remain diagnosable through complete-report verify; failed rollback preserves recovery evidence.
Official CLI readers/writers are coordinated by shared/exclusive OS locks; open write-ahead journals rollback interrupted multi-file writes.
Crash injection after baseline/receipt/state/event writes rolls all four layers back; unexpected post-crash bytes are never overwritten without --force.
Post-axis dev15: recovery fully validates/preflights journals; rogue entries and unexpected post-crash deletions block nondestructive recovery unless force is explicit.
Post-axis: recovery validates full journal semantics before mutation, treats external deletion as conflict, and ignores no rogue transaction entries.
Recognized P6 evidence migrates byte-preserving through a versioned registry; unknown versions are never reset.
Migration detection covers dependency and materialization-only P6 evidence; runtime marker parser matches schema-critical provenance constraints.
Post-axis dev15: migration rejects symlinked/corrupt released evidence; runtime-layout provenance cross-links registry + audit event; schema/runtime contracts agree.
Post-axis: runtime-layout migration provenance is registry-bound; migration rejects symlinked/tampered released evidence and schema/runtime marker constraints match.
10k/50k graph plus 10k diff/render baseline measured; absolute normalized budget intentionally deferred to P8 per Q7.3.
Q7.E8 carries this explicit partial into P8; P8-A8 is blocking before final release acceptance.
Crash subprocess, concurrency, migration, symlink and conflict-recovery regressions exercise failure semantics.
P7 targeted suite covers materialization-only migration, committed cleanup residue, strict marker parsing and external-edit conflict recovery.
Post-axis dev15 regression tests cover corrupt journals, rollback failure, rogue entries, external deletion, migration corruption/provenance and hardening audit-log corruption.
